prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
short answer: there isn’t one universal “best” — the best roofing company for you depends on your roof type, budget, exact location in Miami, and whether you need residential or commercial work. Rather than trusting a single name, choose a roofer with the hurricane-specific credentials and track record below.

What to require for hurricane-rated roof replacement
- Miami‑Dade Product Approval (NOA) approved materials and installation methods (ask for NOA numbers).  
- Florida roofing contractor license (verify on Florida DBPR).  
- Manufacturer certification (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT, TAMKO Pro, etc.).  
- Experience with wind‑uplift assemblies and hurricane straps/clip installations.  
- Written, transferable manufacturer and workmanship warranties (get details in writing).  
- Proof of insurance (GL and workers’ comp) and liability limits.  
- Permits pulled and final inspection handled by the contractor.  
- Positive, recent references and photos of completed hurricane‑rated projects.  
- BBB score/Google/Yelp reviews and no open complaint history.

How to compare bids (ask every contractor)
- Ask them to list materials by brand/part number and provide NOA numbers.  
- Request an itemized estimate (removal, underlayment, flashing, decking repair, fastening schedule, disposal).  
- Get timeline, payment schedule (avoid large up‑front cash payments), and start-to-finish warranty terms.  
- Ask for three recent projects in Miami with contactable references.  
- Verify they will pull permits and schedule final inspections.

Red flags
- Door‑to‑door storm chasers, high‑pressure sales tactics, or dramatically low bids.  
- No license or insurance, no written contract, or only verbal warranties.  
- Refusal to provide NOA numbers or manufacturer certification.

Where to find and verify contractors
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control (NOA database) — verify material/installation approvals.  
- Florida DBPR license lookup — confirm contractor license number and status.  
- BBB, Google Reviews, Angi, Yelp for customer feedback.  
- Manufacturer locators (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning) to find certified installers.

If you want, I can:
- Look up and shortlist top-rated, NOA‑approved roofing contractors near your ZIP code (residential vs commercial).  
- Draft an email or checklist of questions to send to contractors.  

Tell me your ZIP code and whether it’s a home or commercial building and I’ll prepare a short vetted list and sample questions.
